Schema conversion, IO adapter, exact dispatch, writer facade and type checker are now covered; V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 concrete writers and shared structural pipeline are covered separately. The V2_0 writer, testing helpers, exact-version compatibility tests and fixture generator sources are also covered. writer_tests.rs is also fully analyzed. Encoded-file concat compatibility, Blob part validation, page relocation and output lifecycle are now covered. Delegated IO/decoder scheduling, V1 writer and individual binary fixtures remain pending. Frozen V1 projection/mapping, dictionary dispatch, metadata conversion/batch grouping and dense page-table helpers are now covered; their concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are now covered; full V1 reader is now analyzed; V1 writer/statistics and backend lifecycle remain pending.

Imports shared MAGIC, core errors, ObjectStore/Path and exact version. determine_file_version(store,path,known_size)->Result<ConcreteFileVersion> obtains size via await store.size only if unknown, checked-converts it to usize or InvalidInput with path. Supplied usize size is trusted without checking actual length; no explicit size lookup then. Underlying open behavior is delegated, so this does not prove all HEAD requests avoided.

Reject size<8 with InvalidInput source text and path, then await open_with_size and exactly requested range size-8..size. Compare footer[4..] to MAGIC; mismatch returns contextual InvalidInput. No explicit received-length check: fewer than4 returned bytes can panic on slice; other non8 lengths fail magic comparison. Store/range IO errors propagate. No full file parse or schema/page integrity check.

Decode first two little-endian u16 values from four bytes, then delegate ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers. Magic match implies exactly8 returned bytes for this equality check. Unknown version error lacks path because decoder formats just the pair. The helper recognizes accepted footer aliases only and cannot establish complete file validity.

ranges: SPDX and variable-length module header; dependencies provide Arrow arithmetic/casts/builders and byte-array types, buffers, Bytes, ordered futures streams, alignment-aware BufferExt, async Writer/Reader and PlainDecoder for the position array. No current-format registration or version selection occurs here.

Public BinaryEncoder holds a private exclusive borrowed Writer. new only stores that reference; it does not validate writer position, initialize a header or allocate a page. The caller retains writer lifecycle responsibility.

Private generic encode_typed_arr sums logical lengths, reserves N+1 Int64 positions, records current writer position as the first absolute offset, then downcasts every input to the chosen GenericByteArray<T> with unwrap. It uses each sliced array's first and final offsets. Mixed input types can panic after earlier arrays have already been written; lengths, arithmetic and usize-to-i64 conversion are unchecked.

Unsafe from_raw_parts borrows exactly the sliced value-buffer span start..end, writes it, then appends rebased absolute positions for every logical element. Safety relies on valid Arrow offsets/buffers and homogeneous generic arrays; no local check or SAFETY comment enforces the pointer span. Original validity is not serialized or consulted. Null slots with nonzero payload spans therefore cannot be reconstructed as null solely from this output. Each successful write precedes updating local last_offset; later failure has no rollback.

After all payloads, capture positions_offset, write the Int64 values buffer directly and return that table position. No explicit endian conversion, alignment, page header, framing or validity bitmap is emitted. encode asserts a nonempty slice, dispatches solely from the first array to Utf8/Binary/LargeUtf8/LargeBinary and returns InvalidInput with type for all others, including views. A nonempty slice of empty arrays still writes one position; an empty slice panics.

Public BinaryDecoder<T> privately borrows Reader and stores position, logical length, nullable and PhantomData<T>. new is infallible and performs no bounds/type/offset validation. The constructor doc mistakenly links BinaryEncoder and calls position the batch start; the implementation expects the position-table location returned by BinaryEncoder. The example constructs an Utf8 decoder over a local reader but does not execute a read.

get_positions constructs a PlainDecoder<Int64> with length+1, requests index.start..index.end+1 and returns an Arc of the cloned primitive array. Position bounds are delegated to PlainDecoder, and additions are unchecked. This obtains both endpoints for the selected logical range; the complete first-to-last take position span is read at once.

count_nulls allocates validity for offsets.len()-1 elements. Adjacent equal offsets clear validity and increment null count; unequal offsets set it. If none are null the bitmap is discarded. This intentionally conflates empty values with null when nullable=true; nullable=false callers never invoke it. It does not distinguish equal offsets caused by an originally valid empty value.

get_range indexes absolute start/end, slices range.len()+1 positions, subtracts start and casts to Int32 for small-offset byte types; large types retain Int64. It skips payload IO for start>=end, otherwise requests the absolute byte range. The assertion positions.len()>=range.end is weaker than the final endpoint access, which needs range.end<len; private callers must supply that extra endpoint. Negative, nonmonotone, oversized and arithmetic-overflow positions have no explicit local validation; arithmetic/casts/array building may fail later.

Build the requested GenericByteArray with row count, normalized offsets and payload Bytes converted through BufferExt(alignment1). When nullable, validity comes from equal original position pairs. The fallible ArrayDataBuilder::build is the final delegated validation boundary; no local short-response or UTF8 check is separately implemented. Return a new Arc array, potentially sharing the reader-returned payload allocation through BufferExt.

Private Debug TakeChunksPlan holds relative UInt32 indices plus is_contiguous. Planner documentation promises either contiguous nonrepeating indices or nearby values. It subtracts the first input index with Arrow arithmetic, initializes start_idx=0, last_idx=-1 and contiguous=true. Empty input would panic at value(0); public take guards emptiness first. No sort, null rejection or monotonicity validation occurs here.

For each relative current index, curr_contiguous is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1. A noncontiguous item starts a new chunk only when its byte position is strictly more than min_io_size from the current chunk's first index. Otherwise AND the contiguous flag; always update last_idx and finally append the remainder. Continuous runs can exceed the IO threshold. start_idx is an ordinal, so its comparison with a relative row index can classify repeats as contiguous: normalized [0,0] retains true. This is a source-derived discrepancy with the nonrepeating comment, not a runtime reproduction.

decode delegates get(..). Public take documents sorted indices, returns a typed empty array before IO for empty input, otherwise uses first/last values to request the full position span. MIN_IO_SIZE is fixed at 64*1024 bytes; TODOs leave it nonconfigurable and position reads unchunked. end+1 uses u32 arithmetic before conversion. Unsorted, nullable or out-of-bounds indices are not validated here.

Compute exact intended payload capacity by iterating every index, unwrapping its validity and summing adjacent position differences relative to the first index. Null indices panic here. Allocate payload and (N+1)*offset-width buffers, initialize zero offset using unchecked push. The safety comment relies on sufficient precomputed capacity; length/product/difference overflow and negative persisted positions remain unchecked. Duplicate indices contribute their payload lengths repeatedly to capacity.

Plan chunks, issue each enclosing byte-array range through get_range and poll with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism()). A contiguous chunk copies value_data once, while a noncontiguous chunk copies each requested value. Both append a cumulative offset per requested index with unsafe push_unchecked under the capacity assumption. Repeated-leading [k,k] with a nonempty value becomes a contiguous [0,0] chunk: only one value span is copied but two offsets are accumulated. Ordered buffering preserves planned output order; it does not spawn detached tasks or add error/cancellation cleanup.

After IO, build output offsets and debug-assert copied payload bytes equal the precomputed capacity. The repeated-leading nonempty-value trace violates that assertion in debug builds; without it, inconsistent final offsets reach fallible array building. When nullable, equal output offsets again determine validity. Return a new materialized payload array. No guarantee is claimed for malformed inputs or release behavior beyond the observed builder call.

decode_range checks end>logical length first and returns contextual InvalidInput, then accepts any Range::is_empty as a typed empty array. Thus out-of-bounds equal endpoints fail when end is too large, while reversed ranges whose end is in bounds return empty. Otherwise read N+1 positions through PlainDecoder and decode local 0..N. RangeFrom beyond length becomes an empty reversed range after get expands it.

Public get converts ReadBatchParams once: Range, full, to and from become decode_range; Indices delegates take; Ranges returns InvalidInput stating multiple ranges are unsupported. There is no inclusive-range arm, fallback or automatic sorting here.

The cfg(test) module imports string/binary types, concat and local temp-file IO. write_test_data creates/truncates a file, writes four garbage prefix bytes, encodes provided strings and explicitly shuts down before returning table offset. It tests nonzero absolute positions but is a helper, not an independent assertion oracle.

Generic test_round_trips writes strings, opens a 1024-byte-block local reader, decodes nullable=true using summed rows and compares the typed result with Arrow concat of the original arrays. It covers the arrays supplied by callers only; no byte-layout, failure-timing or backend durability assertion is present.

test_write_binary_data runs six Utf8/LargeUtf8 fixtures: basic nonempty values, nullable values and multiple arrays. Nullable examples use None rather than valid empty strings; they do not distinguish empty values from null, cover views, or exercise LargeBinary. All compare decoded contents through the shared helper.

The offset test slices [d,e] to the one-element e view, then runs the string roundtrip helper. It specifically exercises nonzero Arrow value offsets, not arbitrary malformed offsets or multiple sliced inputs.

Range fixture encodes a..g after a four-byte prefix with nullable=false. It asserts decode/full, 2..5, ..5, 4.. and empty 2..2 exact results; 100..100 is only required to return some error. It does not check the error category/message, reversed ranges or a RangeFrom beyond length.
Basic take fixture decodes sorted unique indices [1,2,5] from a..g and requires [b,c,f]. No duplicate, null-index, unsorted or out-of-bounds behavior is tested.

Sparse fixture builds one million strings, checks that a plan for indices [1,999998] yields two relative singleton chunks [0] and [999997], then checks actual decoded values. The planner receives a positions excerpt beginning at1; decoder.take obtains its own endpoints. This is a large source fixture, not evidence of subsecond runtime or measured IO count.

Dense planner fixture uses one million strings and indices [2,3,4,1001,1001,1002,2001,2002,2004,3004,3005] with a 1024-byte threshold. It asserts four exact relative chunks and flags true,false,false,true, distinguishing repeats in the later chunk and gaps. The manually supplied positions begin at1 although the first requested index is2; this fixture's asserted grouping is not a general origin-validation test. Leading repeats such as [2,2] are absent.

The dense fixture separately calls decoder.take with its normal fixed 64KiB planner threshold and checks exact values including the repeated string-1001. That successful oracle does not establish that the preceding 1024-byte plan is used by take, nor cover the leading-repeat fast-path discrepancy.

Write-slice test emits ten slices of ten ten-byte strings and checks only returned positions: i*(8*11)+(i+1)*(10*10). This pins payload-first layout and N+1 Int64 table spacing across repeated calls. It does not read back, shut down explicitly or test nullable slices.

Binary-null take fixture constructs 60000 values, with every fourth null and all others eight bytes. After prefixed write/shutdown it takes [0,5,59996] and requires [None,abcdefgh,None]. A commented debugging fragment has no behavior. The file ends after eight active tests; malformed positions, leading duplicates, empty-vs-null, mixed-array types, partial writes and cancellation lack local tests.

DictionaryEncoder privately borrows a mutable Writer and key DataType. Public new stores both without checking dictionary array shape, supported key type or correspondence with future inputs.

write_typed_array asserts nonempty inputs, records writer position, then downcasts every input using the chosen key type and collects borrowed key arrays. It constructs PlainEncoder using the first original dictionary DataType, but PlainEncoder's non-FSL branch selects actual primitive key type from the arrays. Supported type plus empty input reaches the assertion, whereas unsupported type returns its error without examining the slice. No per-array schema preflight or rollback is added.

Public DictionaryDecoder privately stores Reader, key-page position, logical row count, borrowed dictionary DataType and owned shared value_arr. Its Debug output includes position, length, declared type and full value_arr debug representation, but omits Reader. This can be large; no redaction or abbreviated dictionary is implemented.

new asserts only that data_type is Dictionary, then stores supplied state. It does not check the declared value type against value_arr.data_type, key validity, dictionary cardinality or file bounds. A non-dictionary input panics despite later decode_impl containing an Arrow error branch for that shape.

decode_impl extracts and asserts a dictionary key type, creates PlainDecoder over the key page, and awaits the requested selection. It dispatches the decoded key array over the eight integer types to make_dict_array; unsupported match fallback is Arrow error. Range and take behavior, lost stored validity and read failures inherit PlainDecoder. The expected value type is ignored after extracting the key type.

make_dict_array downcasts/clones the primitive keys and calls fallible DictionaryArray::try_new with a clone of the stored values Arc. This delegates key/value construction validation and shares the existing dictionary values. No values IO or schema-value-type comparison occurs; the resulting dictionary's value type follows the supplied value array. The async helper has no await in its body.

Public decode requests full range, take clones the UInt32Array selector and forwards it, and get forwards arbitrary convertible ReadBatchParams. All converge on decode_impl without another validation layer. No cache, value dictionary merge or independently optimized take is introduced.

The decoder fixture writes those extracted keys with PlainEncoder directly, shuts down, supplies the same values Arc to DictionaryDecoder and compares full decoded dictionary contents with [a,b,b,d]. The sole active test invokes the helper sequentially for Int8/16/32/64 and UInt8/16/32/64. It supplies eight full-decode oracles, not dictionary-encoder, take/range, null-key, mismatched-value-type, invalid-key or incompatible-dictionary coverage. File ends here without unsafe blocks.

ranges: SPDX and module prose describe fixed-stride direct storage and O(1) access. That complexity describes computing a row byte position, not total IO, recursive reconstruction or take allocation. Imports provide raw slices, Arrow arithmetic/layout/buffers/selection, async recursion, ordered streams, local Arrow extensions and Reader/Writer.

PlainEncoder stores borrowed Writer and configured DataType; new performs no validation. Static write records tell, returns that position without encoding for an empty array slice, otherwise chooses the first array type and encodes. Instance encode delegates recursively even for an empty slice and can reach an assertion. Its comment calls the return a metadata offset, but primitive implementation returns the raw values start; no separate plain metadata is emitted.

encode_internal branches only on configured FixedSizeList, delegating its item Field; every other configured type goes to encode_primitive, which reads the actual first input type. async_recursion boxes recursive calls. This distinction explains why DictionaryEncoder can configure a dictionary type while passing primitive key arrays. No general configured-vs-actual type check exists.

encode_boolean reserves summed logical length, iterates every input value, replaces None with false and appends values to one BooleanBuilder. It writes only the finished values bitmap, eliminating byte-padding gaps between short arrays. No validity bitmap is written, so null booleans read as valid false. Allocation and iteration are proportional to total input rows.

encode_primitive asserts a nonempty slice and captures writer position. Boolean inputs are downcast and packed; other inputs use the first type's byte_width for every raw buffer slice, starting at each array offset and writing len*width bytes. No endian conversion, validity, per-array type/buffer-length check, alignment padding or rollback. Unsafe from_raw_parts requires each computed span to remain inside a valid allocation across await; mixed narrower arrays can violate that safety precondition. Existing Arrow validity alone does not establish homogeneous inputs.

encode_fixed_size_list downcasts each input or returns Schema with actual type, slices its child values from value_offset(0) for len*value_length, collects shared child arrays and recurses using configured items.data_type. Parent nulls are discarded, as are child validity buffers once primitive encoding occurs. Actual list sizes and configured item type are not compared here; casts/products and recursion depth are unchecked. A failure can follow already-written data in nested/earlier operations.

PlainDecoder privately borrows Reader and DataType and stores position/length. get_byte_range maps booleans to floor(start/8)..ceil(end/8), otherwise multiplies endpoints by byte_width. All byte-offset arithmetic is unchecked. The locally defined DataTypeExt::byte_width panics when width is unavailable; FixedSizeList<Boolean> has no scalar byte width for the take planner (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182).

bytes_to_array requires Arrow layout.buffers.len()==1 or returns Internal with type. FixedWidth computes (len+offset).saturating_mul(width); a short Bytes response is copied into that minimum size with zero fill, otherwise BufferExt may retain aligned Bytes or copy misaligned bytes. Non-FixedWidth layouts copy from the byte slice. The len+offset addition itself is unchecked; this helper does not reject truncation for fixed-width values. BufferExt behavior is established at rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600.

ArrayDataBuilder constructs the declared type with requested len/offset, null_count0 and one value buffer, then fallibly builds and make_array returns an ArrayRef. All restored rows are valid at this layer. Public PlainDecoder::new returns Result but unconditionally constructs Ok and does not enforce fixed stride, positive dimensions, file bounds or schema compatibility.

decode_primitive rejects only end>length, computes absolute file byte range, awaits Reader::get_range, and reconstructs with bit offset start%8 for booleans or0 otherwise. It relies on decode_range to remove empty/reversed ranges. Short fixed-width responses may be zero-padded by bytes_to_array; exact response length is not independently checked. Position additions, byte multiplication and end-start subtraction are unchecked.

Fixed-size-list decoding requires the item type satisfy local is_fixed_stride or returns Schema. It constructs a child decoder with length*list_size and requests scaled endpoints, then uses FixedSizeListArray::new with cloned item Field and parent validity None. Nested fixed lists are allowed by the predicate and recurse. Signed sizes are cast unchecked and products are unchecked; zero/negative dimensions and constructor panic behavior are not locally guarded.

Fixed-size-binary decoding treats values as UInt8 with length*stride, requests scaled endpoints, downcasts or returns Schema, then delegates to FixedSizeBinaryArrayExt::try_new_from_values. The helper sets len=values.len()/stride and builds from the value buffer without validity (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:455-463). Zero stride can reach division by zero; negative dimensions and overflow are not locally validated.

Boolean take casts reader.block_size to u32, multiplies by8 and partitions sorted selector ordinals when the next row enters a higher block than the chunk's first row. It assumes nonempty input, which public take guards. Zero/truncated block size can cause division by zero, and multiplication/ordinal casts are unchecked. Selector validity and sortedness are not examined.

For each boolean chunk, read its enclosing first..last+1 row range, subtract the first row from the UInt32 selector and invoke Arrow take. Poll ordered futures with reader.io_parallelism, collect every decoded chunk array, then concatenate. This allocates intermediate arrays plus final output, preserves chunk order and delegates nullable-index selection to Arrow after planning from raw values. No detached spawn or local cancellation guard is present.

make_chunked_requests returns ordinal ranges into a nonempty sorted index slice. Adjacent consecutive rows always stay together even if the run exceeds block_size; otherwise split only when next*width is strictly greater than first*width+block_size. The comment about limiting IO is therefore not a hard cap. It uses usize byte arithmetic but unchecked u32 previous+1 and unchecked products/sums; empty input underflows len-1.

decode delegates the full logical range. take returns an empty typed array before type checks/IO, routes Boolean specially, otherwise computes byte_width and chunks raw indices.values using reader.block_size. No sort, bound preflight, null rejection or normalization occurs. FixedSizeList<Boolean> can decode by range but its take path reaches the byte_width panic; the constructor does not prevent that combination.

For each ordinary take chunk, read enclosing first..last+1, shift its selector by the first row, run Arrow take, collect ordered buffered results and concat. Duplicates in valid sorted selectors are preserved by Arrow take; unsorted or nullable selector storage can affect the planned enclosing range before Arrow processes validity. Reads can cover intervening unselected rows and contiguous runs larger than block_size. All chunk arrays remain alive until final concatenation.

decode_range returns new_empty_array immediately for Range::is_empty, before any bounds/type validation. Thus even an empty range beyond length or a reversed range is accepted. Nonempty fixed lists/binary delegate recursive reconstruction; everything else goes to primitive. This differs from BinaryDecoder, which checks end before empty-range return.

get converts the parameter once; Range/full/to/from route to decode_range, Indices to take, and Ranges returns InvalidInput saying multiple ranges are unsupported. There is no per-selection extra type/bounds check. A RangeFrom start beyond length becomes reversed and returns empty.

Narrow integers reinterpret portions of the i64 buffer; this is not a cast preserving the mathematical sequence1..126. Every case uses the shared roundtrip oracle.

The same test generates126 random f64 values, reinterprets their bytes as Float16/32/64 arrays and runs ten-array roundtrips. It tests raw-buffer roundtrip, not equivalent numerical values across float widths, deterministic fixtures or all NaN/Infinity semantics. No runtime timing evidence was gathered.

test_round_trip writes arrays, requires returned offset0, flushes and drops writer, opens a reader, requires positive file size, decodes summed row count, compares with Arrow concat and asserts resulting length. It checks in-process local contents only, without pinned bytes, nonzero offsets, error injection or durable backend guarantees.
Boolean roundtrip uses ten length3 arrays of true values. It covers joining arrays whose lengths are not byte-aligned, but no false/null values, sliced bit offsets or boolean take.

Fixed-size-list test runs eight integer item types with list size3 and ten arrays per type, using the same reinterpreted i64 buffer and the local list constructor. Shared roundtrip checks equality and count. Parent/item nulls, sliced lists, invalid sizes and child types outside this matrix are absent.

FixedSizeBinary(3) roundtrip creates ten arrays over UInt8 values1..127 and checks them through the shared helper. It tests a positive divisible stride and no nulls, not malformed zero/negative strides or nondivisible input.

Padding fixture passes five bytes [1,0,2,0,3] to bytes_to_array(UInt16,len3,offset0), asserts values [1,2,3] and a Debug buffer substring [1,0,2,0,3,0]. This directly pins zero extension and the fixture's byte interpretation, not rejection of truncated input or portable endian conversion.
Nested fixture roundtrips ten arrays of FixedSizeList<FixedSizeList<Int64,2>,2> built from120 values. It exercises recursive encoder/decoder flattening but no nulls or slices.

The second nested fixture uses FixedSizeList<FixedSizeBinary(2),2> over120 UInt8 values with ten arrays. It confirms the fixed-binary child branch through the same full-read oracle, not boolean children or take.

Async make_array_ simply builds a len126 array of the requested type over a clone of a supplied raw buffer and unwraps; it has no await. That deliberate reinterpretation is why the primitive matrix is a buffer-roundtrip test rather than a numeric-conversion test.

This protects usize byte arithmetic on a sufficiently wide host, not checked overflow or u32::MAX row indices. read_binary_array is public async with borrowed Reader/DataType, nullable, byte position, logical length and generic Into<ReadBatchParams>. It converts params first, then Utf8 instantiates BinaryDecoder<Utf8Type> and awaits get. Offset/range/null/layout validation and IO are delegated to the concrete decoder, not added here.

Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary dispatch to their corresponding Arrow generic BinaryDecoder. Any other type gives InvalidInput with displayed data_type. This exact four-type set is narrower than local DataTypeExt::is_binary_like, which also includes Utf8View/BinaryView; therefore passing the broad binary-like predicate does not guarantee successful dispatch.

read_fixed_stride_array first checks DataTypeExt::is_fixed_stride and returns Schema error with type if false. LanceFileVersion is a caller selector with Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. FromStr lowercases but does not trim. Accepted aliases are0.1/legacy,2.0/0.3,2.1,2.2,2.3,stable,next. ## Footer detection and errors

determine_file_version takes ObjectStore,Path,optional known usize size. If unknown, await store.size and checked-convert; if known, trust it. Reject size<8, await open_with_size and get_range(size-8..size), require footer[4..]==LANC, decode first four bytes as LEu16 major/minor and dispatch exact parser. IO errors propagate; size/magic/version errors are InvalidInput. Fewer than4 returned bytes could panic because no explicit received-length check precedes slicing. ## Ownership and integration

Each encoder exclusively borrows Writer; each decoder borrows Reader. Plain and dictionary codecs also borrow DataType, while BinaryDecoder selects the Arrow byte-array type through its generic parameter and stores nullable. DictionaryDecoder owns an ArrayRef for already loaded values. Constructors store state without general file-bound or schema validation; DictionaryDecoder::new asserts the outer dictionary shape, and PlainDecoder::new unconditionally returns Ok. ## Binary layout and null semantics

For N rows, write the sliced payload spans in order, then N+1 absolute Int64 byte positions. Return the position-table start, not the first payload byte. The first position is Writer::tell before payloads; later array offsets are rebased to the current absolute end. The raw Int64 buffer is written without explicit endian conversion or framing. A nonempty list of empty arrays writes one endpoint; an empty input slice asserts. Exactly Utf8, Binary, LargeUtf8 and LargeBinary are supported; views return InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105)

The encoder ignores original validity. Decoder nullable=true marks equal adjacent positions null, so valid empty values become null and null slots retaining nonempty payload cannot be distinguished from valid values. nullable=false returns all values valid, including empty spans. This is a frozen representation rule, not a universal null-preserving binary codec. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:61-86; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-232)

Range reads first fetch N+1 Int64 positions through PlainDecoder, subtract the first absolute position and cast offsets to Int32 for small byte arrays. Payload IO is skipped when start>=end; otherwise request that absolute byte range. Array construction is fallible, but negative/nonmonotone offsets and exact response size have no dedicated local checks. The internal endpoint assertion is weaker than the subsequent endpoint access. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:153-233; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-415)

## Selection rules and IO cost

| Behavior | BinaryDecoder | PlainDecoder and dictionary key reads |
|---|---|---|
| Empty range beyond logical length | Reject if end exceeds length before empty check | Return empty before bounds/type checks |
| Reversed range with end in bounds | Return empty | Return empty |
| RangeFrom starting beyond length | Return empty reversed range | Return empty reversed range |
| Multiple Ranges | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |
| Empty Indices | Typed empty, no IO | Typed empty, no IO |
| Take planning | Full first-to-last position span; fixed 64KiB byte-distance threshold | Reader block size; Boolean-specific block arithmetic |
| Ordering validation | Sorted-input assumption, no sorting; null index unwraps during sizing | Raw selector values drive planning without sorting or null preflight |

Selection evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:286-328; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-428; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-343; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:374-439; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:122-174.

Binary takes precompute the sum of selected value lengths, allocate payload and N+1 offsets, read planned chunks with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), then copy a contiguous chunk once or gather each requested value. The position span can be large for two far-apart rows; a contiguous value run can exceed the nominal 64KiB threshold. Output is materialized even when the range-reader payload can share Bytes storage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:246-390)

Plain takes keep consecutive rows in the same chunk regardless of block_size, and otherwise split by distance from the chunk's first row. Boolean takes split on row/(block_size*8). Both read enclosing ranges, apply Arrow take and retain all decoded chunk arrays before concat. The IO threshold is not a maximum request size; zero/truncated Boolean block sizes and unchecked arithmetic remain assumptions. FixedSizeList<Boolean> range decoding can recurse, while take calls byte_width, which is unavailable for its Boolean child. ## Repeated-leading-index discrepancy

The binary planner's condition is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1, where current is a relative row index and start_idx is a selector ordinal. For a nonempty value of length L and sorted indices [k,k], subtraction gives [0,0]; both iterations satisfy current==start_idx, leaving is_contiguous=true. The chunk reads/copies one value span L, but the output offsets and capacity count two values, reaching the debug assertion L==2L. Release execution reaches fallible array building with inconsistent offsets. This is an explicit source trace, not an executed reproduction. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:251-284; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-388)

The dense test includes a repeated later index and checks correct output; it does not include a repeated first index. Its standalone planner uses a 1024-byte threshold, whereas decoder.take uses 64KiB. Do not generalize that passing fixture into all-duplicate correctness or assume the tested standalone plan is the actual take plan. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:616-662)

## Plain bytes, recursive arrays and unsafe boundaries

Plain primitives write values only. Boolean inputs are joined bit by bit and None becomes false; other types use first-array byte_width and each array's offset/length to form an unsafe raw buffer slice. The configured DataType only selects FixedSizeList recursion; the primitive branch otherwise uses the actual first array type. It never validates that every later array has that type or enough bytes for the resulting span. Homogeneous valid Arrow arrays are a safety precondition: mixed narrower arrays can make the computed raw slice exceed its allocation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-152)

Fixed lists recursively write sliced child values, discarding parent and eventual primitive validity. Read reconstructs them with parent validity None; fixed binary reads UInt8 values then builds a width-based array. Signed dimensions are cast and multiplied without local validation. Null primitive payloads are whatever the input values buffer contains, except Boolean's explicit false substitution; the compatibility fixture's zero/null-key expectations do not prove every possible null backing value is zero. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-304; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135)

bytes_to_array requires one value buffer. For FixedWidth, a short response is copied and zero-filled to (len+offset)*width; otherwise aligned Bytes can be retained and misaligned Bytes are copied. The resulting array has null_count0. This means truncated fixed-width input is not necessarily rejected: the active test supplies five bytes for three UInt16 values and expects the missing sixth byte to be zero. Bit-packed Boolean uses its separate buffer branch and starting bit offset. ## Dictionary keys and values

DictionaryEncoder supports all eight signed/unsigned integer key widths. It extracts each array's keys and writes them with PlainEncoder; no value comparison, dictionary merge/remap, value persistence or key-validity bitmap occurs. Supplying different dictionaries with the same key width therefore requires the caller to have already established compatible key meaning. The constructor's configured key type controls downcasts; unsupported types return Schema and supported types with an empty slice assert. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-77)

DictionaryDecoder reads keys using PlainDecoder, clones the shared values Arc and calls DictionaryArray::try_new. Its declared dictionary value type is never compared with the supplied array; result value type follows that array. Keys lose stored validity through plain reconstruction, but dictionary values can independently be null. The one local test writes keys directly using PlainEncoder and never invokes DictionaryEncoder. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:104-174; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

The foundation's binary-like predicate includes views, but both concrete binary encode and facade decode reject them. PlainEncoder can write fixed-width numeric buffers beyond integer widths, whereas schema dictionary hydration explicitly accepts only eight integer value types or the four binary families. These are different boundaries; do not infer symmetric hydration from write dispatch. ## Ownership and integration

Each encoder exclusively borrows Writer; each decoder borrows Reader. Plain and dictionary codecs also borrow DataType, while BinaryDecoder selects the Arrow byte-array type through its generic parameter and stores nullable. DictionaryDecoder owns an ArrayRef for already loaded values. Constructors store state without general file-bound or schema validation; DictionaryDecoder::new asserts the outer dictionary shape, and PlainDecoder::new unconditionally returns Ok. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:38-47; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:107-151; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:32-42; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:211-224; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-36; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:80-120)

~~~text
V1 writer page adapter
|-- PlainEncoder: primitive bytes / joined Boolean bits / recursive FSL values
|-- BinaryEncoder: payload bytes -> absolute Int64 position table
`-- DictionaryEncoder: PlainEncoder for keys only

V1 reader page adapter
|-- PlainDecoder: range IO -> array reconstruction
|-- BinaryDecoder: PlainDecoder positions -> payload range(s)
`-- DictionaryDecoder: PlainDecoder keys + supplied dictionary values
~~~

The page adapters store the encoder return as PageInfo.position and summed logical rows as length. Dictionary values travel separately through schema dictionary hydration; the reader adapter unwraps both dictionary metadata and loaded values before constructing its decoder. Complete caller lifecycle is not established by these narrow functions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:406-459; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:625-668; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-192)

## Binary layout and null semantics

For N rows, write the sliced payload spans in order, then N+1 absolute Int64 byte positions. Return the position-table start, not the first payload byte. The first position is Writer::tell before payloads; later array offsets are rebased to the current absolute end. The raw Int64 buffer is written without explicit endian conversion or framing. A nonempty list of empty arrays writes one endpoint; an empty input slice asserts. Exactly Utf8, Binary, LargeUtf8 and LargeBinary are supported; views return InvalidInput. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:48-105)

The encoder ignores original validity. Decoder nullable=true marks equal adjacent positions null, so valid empty values become null and null slots retaining nonempty payload cannot be distinguished from valid values. nullable=false returns all values valid, including empty spans. This is a frozen representation rule, not a universal null-preserving binary codec. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:61-86; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-232)

Range reads first fetch N+1 Int64 positions through PlainDecoder, subtract the first absolute position and cast offsets to Int32 for small byte arrays. Payload IO is skipped when start>=end; otherwise request that absolute byte range. Array construction is fallible, but negative/nonmonotone offsets and exact response size have no dedicated local checks. The internal endpoint assertion is weaker than the subsequent endpoint access. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:153-233; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-415)

## Selection rules and IO cost

| Behavior | BinaryDecoder | PlainDecoder and dictionary key reads |
|---|---|---|
| Empty range beyond logical length | Reject if end exceeds length before empty check | Return empty before bounds/type checks |
| Reversed range with end in bounds | Return empty | Return empty |
| RangeFrom starting beyond length | Return empty reversed range | Return empty reversed range |
| Multiple Ranges | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |
| Empty Indices | Typed empty, no IO | Typed empty, no IO |
| Take planning | Full first-to-last position span; fixed 64KiB byte-distance threshold | Reader block size; Boolean-specific block arithmetic |
| Ordering validation | Sorted-input assumption, no sorting; null index unwraps during sizing | Raw selector values drive planning without sorting or null preflight |

Selection evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:286-328; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:394-428; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-343; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:374-439; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:122-174.

Binary takes precompute the sum of selected value lengths, allocate payload and N+1 offsets, read planned chunks with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism), then copy a contiguous chunk once or gather each requested value. The position span can be large for two far-apart rows; a contiguous value run can exceed the nominal 64KiB threshold. Output is materialized even when the range-reader payload can share Bytes storage. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:246-390)

Plain takes keep consecutive rows in the same chunk regardless of block_size, and otherwise split by distance from the chunk's first row. Boolean takes split on row/(block_size*8). Both read enclosing ranges, apply Arrow take and retain all decoded chunk arrays before concat. The IO threshold is not a maximum request size; zero/truncated Boolean block sizes and unchecked arithmetic remain assumptions. FixedSizeList<Boolean> range decoding can recurse, while take calls byte_width, which is unavailable for its Boolean child. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:306-408; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:144-182)

## Repeated-leading-index discrepancy

The binary planner's condition is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1, where current is a relative row index and start_idx is a selector ordinal. For a nonempty value of length L and sorted indices [k,k], subtraction gives [0,0]; both iterations satisfy current==start_idx, leaving is_contiguous=true. The chunk reads/copies one value span L, but the output offsets and capacity count two values, reaching the debug assertion L==2L. Release execution reaches fallible array building with inconsistent offsets. This is an explicit source trace, not an executed reproduction. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:251-284; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:309-388)

The dense test includes a repeated later index and checks correct output; it does not include a repeated first index. Its standalone planner uses a 1024-byte threshold, whereas decoder.take uses 64KiB. Do not generalize that passing fixture into all-duplicate correctness or assume the tested standalone plan is the actual take plan. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:616-662)

## Plain bytes, recursive arrays and unsafe boundaries

Plain primitives write values only. Boolean inputs are joined bit by bit and None becomes false; other types use first-array byte_width and each array's offset/length to form an unsafe raw buffer slice. The configured DataType only selects FixedSizeList recursion; the primitive branch otherwise uses the actual first array type. It never validates that every later array has that type or enough bytes for the resulting span. Homogeneous valid Arrow arrays are a safety precondition: mixed narrower arrays can make the computed raw slice exceed its allocation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:60-152)

Fixed lists recursively write sliced child values, discarding parent and eventual primitive validity. Read reconstructs them with parent validity None; fixed binary reads UInt8 values then builds a width-based array. Signed dimensions are cast and multiplied without local validation. Null primitive payloads are whatever the input values buffer contains, except Boolean's explicit false substitution; the compatibility fixture's zero/null-key expectations do not prove every possible null backing value is zero. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:73-152; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:252-304; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135)

bytes_to_array requires one value buffer. For FixedWidth, a short response is copied and zero-filled to (len+offset)*width; otherwise aligned Bytes can be retained and misaligned Bytes are copied. The resulting array has null_count0. This means truncated fixed-width input is not necessarily rejected: the active test supplies five bytes for three UInt16 values and expects the missing sixth byte to be zero. Bit-packed Boolean uses its separate buffer branch and starting bit offset. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:174-249; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:575-592; rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:1536-1600)

These codecs perform unchecked pointer/offset/capacity arithmetic and have assertions/downcasts in public-call paths. No local transaction, rollback, flush/shutdown, abort guard or cancellation cleanup appears. Buffered futures preserve order and limit polling concurrency but do not prove backend cancellation; complete IO ownership remains pending. ## Dictionary keys and values

DictionaryEncoder supports all eight signed/unsigned integer key widths. It extracts each array's keys and writes them with PlainEncoder; no value comparison, dictionary merge/remap, value persistence or key-validity bitmap occurs. Supplying different dictionaries with the same key width therefore requires the caller to have already established compatible key meaning. The constructor's configured key type controls downcasts; unsupported types return Schema and supported types with an empty slice assert. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:26-77)

DictionaryDecoder reads keys using PlainDecoder, clones the shared values Arc and calls DictionaryArray::try_new. Its declared dictionary value type is never compared with the supplied array; result value type follows that array. Keys lose stored validity through plain reconstruction, but dictionary values can independently be null. The one local test writes keys directly using PlainEncoder and never invokes DictionaryEncoder. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:104-174; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:187-252)

The foundation's binary-like predicate includes views, but both concrete binary encode and facade decode reject them. PlainEncoder can write fixed-width numeric buffers beyond integer widths, whereas schema dictionary hydration explicitly accepts only eight integer value types or the four binary families. These are different boundaries; do not infer symmetric hydration from write dispatch. # Frozen V1 foundations: projection, dictionaries, metadata and page tables

Complete local scope: five files / 854 physical lines, including five tests. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered in the [codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md); full V1 reader/writer/statistics and binary fixtures remain pending. [Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Current composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [V2_0 and compatibility](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
`-- reader / writer / writer/statistics: full lifecycle pending
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. A narrow V1 writer footer trace writes data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata, then magics; full provider/finish/error lifecycle is not established by that snippet. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. Complete reader validation/lifecycle remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Two metadata tests assert one index-group example and four valid range splits. Three page-table tests assert set/get, missing-cell zeros after write/read and three error variants/messages. The roundtrip test starts expected from actual.clone and overwrites fourteen holes; six populated values lack independent expectations. No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:209-255) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:162-287) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:186-192) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:102-116)
